description: Analyze the throughput scaling law as SIMD vector width doubles from 128 to 256 to 512 to 1024+ bits. Each doubling doubles data per instruction but may introduce cross-lane costs and frequency throttling. Determine the optimal vector width for Base64 decode on current and projected hardware.
mathematical_formalization: T(w) = (w/8 * 3/4) / (C_lookup(w) + C_pack(w) + C_compact(w) + C_overhead(w)) bytes/cycle. SSE: T~0.86 B/c. AVX2: T~1.71 B/c. AVX-512: T~4.8 B/c. AVX-512-VBMI: T~6.86 B/c. Scaling is super-linear due to unlocking better instructions at wider widths.
analogical_connections: GPU compute: warp width affects occupancy and register pressure
Amdahl's law: serial fraction limits speedup from wider vectors
DRAM bandwidth: wider vectors approach bandwidth limits faster
implementation_hypothesis: Implement decode at SSE4.2, AVX2, AVX-512BW, AVX-512VBMI widths with identical structure. Plot throughput vs width. Measure frequency throttling impact.
experiment_seed: Run benchmarks on Sapphire Rapids, Haswell, Zen4, Apple M2. Plot GB/s vs vector width. Correlate with uarch events.
